Prompts: REA_17 §3.4. · edge (catalyst pole only; owner 2026-10-16, THE EDGE v9: two sentences, the energy and its three ruling domains from the GOD table, then a clause per domain in The Pattern's voice; the metric; the head derived in the app)

candidates.structural_interaction: Wood pressing Earth same-polarity — the destabilising reach that roots break stone
candidates.k2_overview: Your Wood moves as the General: growth under discipline. Your ambition climbs like bamboo, fast, segmented, unstoppable, turning pressure into height. You command by growing first, taking the arrows meant for everyone behind you. Just remember trees also bend. The rigid campaign is the one that snaps.
candidates.k2_functional: Your discipline is a strict coach: cut the extras, keep the goal, hold the line for years.

k2_domain_readings.Pressure: Pressure accelerates your growth: deadlines, competition, expectation all read as sunlight. Choose pressures that build height, and shed the ones that only strip bark.
k2_domain_readings.Command: You command by example and altitude: first up, most exposed, setting pace. It inspires and it isolates. Grow lieutenants deliberately so the canopy is not one tree.
k2_domain_readings.Crisis: In crisis you are the tree others shelter under: bending, holding, regrowing what storms take. After each one, tend your own roots first. Shelter has a maintenance cost.

catalyst.define: As a catalyst, the world asks too little of your strength. It wakes fully only when something real is at stake.

angles.drive: Your head is clearest when something presses on you. Pressure gives your stored strength a direction, so you look for a hard deadline rather than a quiet week. On a bad day, people steady themselves on your calm.
angles.cost_self: You think clearest under pressure and drift without it. Since calm gives you nothing to press against, you let the easy weeks pass rather than use them. Your best ideas sit idle between one emergency and the next.
angles.cost_others: When things go wrong, your head stays clear. Because calm makes you restless, you bring a crisis pace home rather than let ordinary days run slow. Everyone you live with moves at your speed, even on a lazy Sunday.

angles.drive: You take charge before anyone asks you to. Being out in front settles you, so you would rather take charge than wait to be chosen. In a stalled meeting, your first move gets everyone else going.
angles.cost_self: Taking charge comes to you faster than asking for help. Since staying in charge feels safe, you carry the whole plan rather than hand half over. The weight of everything you run lands on your shoulders alone.
angles.cost_others: Anything half yours, you take charge of as if it were whole. Being in charge is how you show care, and you decide for people before asking them. Those close to you get looked after and seldom get a say.

angles.drive: Where most plans would stop, you push through. Because quitting feels like weakness, you would rather push through than choose to rest. Much of what gets done around you gets done because you stayed.
angles.cost_self: Pushing through is the only pace you trust. A pause reads to you as giving in, and you would rather finish worn out than stop halfway and rested. Your body keeps the bill for every hard mile.
angles.cost_others: You push through and expect the people beside you to push through too. Because slowing down feels like letting them down, you keep the pace high instead of asking who is tired. With you, whole teams reach finish lines they would have walked away from.

friction.define: As a friction, the demands outgrow your strength and the pressure turns inward. Even an hour of ease begins to feel unearned.

angles.drive: You are hard on yourself in ways you would spare a friend. Every slip feels like a test you failed, and the blame lands on you. You are allowed the same mercy you show the people you love.
angles.cost_self: To you, being hard on yourself is the honest way to improve. You put every slip on trial in your head, so you replay the mistake instead of resting once the work is done. You pay for it in the rest you never take.
angles.cost_others: Being hard on yourself does not stay inside you. Since you treat your own slips as weakness, you hold the people close to you to the same rule more than you say. You teach them to hide their small mistakes from you.

angles.drive: You never switch off once the day is done. Wood keeps pressing on a core that has little left, so you read a quiet evening as slipping rather than resting. You have every right to switch off and let the evening be rest.
angles.cost_self: Being needed feels safer than being idle, so you never switch off. Every answered call proves you matter, and you keep the job open in your head instead of closing it. You trade your sleep for that open job and never get the hours back.
angles.cost_others: Never switching off means the people at home get you half there. Because the next demand wins over the evening in front of you, you answer it ahead of them without noticing. At home, you give them whatever the day did not use.

angles.drive: You are never satisfied, not even with yourself. Pressure is how you show you take a thing seriously, so you hold back the pleased look instead of giving it. You are allowed to be pleased by a standard you have already met.
angles.cost_self: Never being satisfied makes help hard to accept. Since good enough never feels safe to you, you redo what you are handed rather than let it please you. You end up carrying alone the work you would not let anyone share.
angles.cost_others: Where you believe in someone, nothing they do ever quite satisfies you. Because you want them at their best, you pass on the strain as much as the standard. It costs them their ease, and they keep guessing what would please you.

retired_2026-09-20_batch3.fn_reading.friction.Overdriven.outside: Watching you rest makes other people anxious, because you do it like a task with a deadline. Friends have stopped suggesting you slow down and started placing quiet bets on when the crash lands. The bets have gotten shorter every year. Nobody says so at dinner.
retired_2026-09-20_batch3.k2_functional: Your discipline is espalier: severe training, few branches, everything bent toward the chosen wall.

edge.lead: Wood runs through your career, your health and your growth. It is the hard stretch at work that feels smaller once begun, the mornings you train for a day not yet here, and the pressure that finds you calm when others shake.
